messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Subject: Hyperscaler cost delta playbook — post-demo recap & next steps

John — thanks for the time today. Quick recap and the concrete asks we agreed on during the demo so nothing falls through the cracks:

1) What we heard on your side
- Primary goal: reduce inference unit cost for customer-facing chat (latency SLO: 150–200ms p95).
- Current baseline: Acme runs comparable models on Hyperscaler X managed endpoints; main pain is variable egress costs + low prefix reuse due to multi-tenant prompts.
- Decision criteria: per-1M token economics, predictable latency under burst, and procurement friendliness (SLA + simple pricing).

2) Redwood differentiators (call highlights)
- Predictable per-token unit economics with reserved (Dedicated) vs hosted fallback routing; automatic prefix/KV caching to reduce upstream token counts.
- Runtime-level batching + quantization profiles we can tune per workload to hit p95 SLO while trimming cost.
- Transparent TCO breakdown (tokens, infra, egress) — we’ll provide a line-item compare to Hyperscaler X.

3) Agreed next tests (we discussed sequencing on the call):
- Synthetic 1M-token TCO model (assumptions attached) — Redwood to deliver per-1M token cost under two configs: hosted standard and dedicated pooled GPUs.
- Batching sensitivity run: 50k–500k concurrent small requests to measure effective latency and throughput and simulated batching efficiency (attached sim settings).
- Cache-hit sensitivity: replays to estimate % token savings with 10%, 25%, 50% prefix reuse (see cache-hit-sensitivity.pdf).

4) Timeline & owners
- Redwood will deliver the 1M-token TCO workbook by EOD tomorrow (Vivek / Ben).
- Benchmark window: Wed–Thu this week for batching sims (Marissa to coordinate test harness).
- Procurement intro: please loop in procurement@acme-ai.com when you’re ready; we’ll prepare a draft reserved-capacity term sheet after the initial econ numbers.

Attachments: acme_1M_token_tco_estimate.xlsx (workbook), batching-sim-settings.json (sim knobs), cache-hit-sensitivity.pdf (assumptions + charts).

Next step: John — confirm procurement contact (or forward this thread) and confirm you’re OK with Redwood running the scheduled synthetic runs Wed–Thu.

Thanks — looking forward to making the comparison concrete.

— Vivek

Thanks Vivek — solid recap. A few clarifying items before we authorize the runs:

1) Data residency: some of our EU customers require tokens/metadata to stay in-region. For the hosted comparison, can you confirm region-specific pricing assumptions or note when an EU-hosted run is required?

2) Throughput target: our production peak is ~350 RPS with an average request size ~60 tokens out / 15 tokens in. Will your batching sim cover a ~300–400 RPS steady-state plus 30% burst tests?

3) TCO baseline: can you show both raw per-1M token cost and an effective cost factoring in cache hits (so we can compare apples-to-apples with our Hyperscaler X numbers which already include some caching savings) — that’s critical for procurement.

If those are covered, please go ahead and run the tests Wed; I’ll loop procurement in this thread (they’ll want the workbook + a simple one-page estimate).

— John

John — short answers to your items + attached workbook has the line-by-line tabs:

1) Region-specific assumptions: workbook has separate tabs for US vs EU egress and reserved capacity pricing. For the hosted numbers in the first tab we assume US region; switching to EU increases egress by ~0.6c/1k tokens in our model (details in tab 'region_assumptions').

2) Throughput / batching: yes — the batching-sim-settings.json that Vivek attached includes tests at 300, 350, 400 RPS with 30% burst windows; our harness uses request-size distribution 15 in / 60 out by default. Expect p95 latency projections for each config in the 'batching_results' tab.

3) Cache-adjusted effective cost: workbook includes a 'cache_adjusted' sheet that computes per-1M token effective cost at variable cache hit rates (10/25/50%). We also include a 'hyperscaler_reference' sheet where we normalize Hyperscaler X published numbers to the same assumptions so procurement can compare directly.

Quick headline from tab 'summary':
- Hosted baseline (US): $42.50 per 1M tokens (no cache).
- Hosted effective at 25% cache: $33.00 per 1M tokens.
- Dedicated reserved pool (40% utilization assumed): $18.75 per 1M tokens (cache-adjusted 25% => $15.50).

Those are modeled numbers — live runs Wed–Thu will produce empirical latency and effective batching savings to validate them.

Attaching: acme_1M_token_tco_estimate.xlsx (detailed workbook).

— Ben
